## Three-axis assessment

### Correctness

**PASSED** — PASSED AFTER REPAIR. The finite-level arithmetic is consistent with the archived PARI transcript: K0 has C3 generated by either prime over 3; K1 has cyclic C63 with prime classes 7 and 56 of exact order 9, so its S-class 3-part vanishes; and, conditional on the uncertified K2 BNF output, each reported prime class has exact order 27 and generates the full 3-Sylow. The original headline’s further claim that this finite prefix “obstructs lambda_fine=3” is not a theorem: finitely many initial vanishing quotients do not determine eventual Iwasawa growth. The repair removes that inference completely.

### Originality

**PASSED** — The retained exact finite-level dataset appears original at the parameter level. LMFDB covers the base class number, while the literature checked gives general fine-Selmer/control and logarithmic-class theory rather than the field-specific K1/K2 class groups, decomposition-prime orders, capitulation, S-quotients, and bnflog outputs recorded here.

### Scientific value

**PASSED** — After narrowing, the result remains a useful exact computational benchmark for the cyclotomic tower of Q(sqrt(-83)) at p=3: it separates unconditional K0/K1 data from conditional K2 data and records the decomposition-prime generation pattern without overinterpreting it. Such finite-level data can constrain and test future control-theorem or characteristic-ideal calculations.
